citation_details.title: Disentangling Confusable Actions in Multimodal HAR: A Stability-driven Feature Selection Framework for EEG and EMG-IMU
citation_details.author: Le Hoang Nhat Do, Ngoc Tuong Vy Le, Quoc Thai Le, Quoc Bao Trinh, Phi Hoai Nguyen, Nhat Ngoc Nguyen, Nhat Tan Le
citation_details.venue: 2026 International Conference on Activity and Behavior Computing (ABC)
citation_details.abstract: Upper-limb movement intention recognition from multimodal biological signals is a key enabling technology for motor-assistive systems and human-computer interaction, yet remains challenged by action ambiguity and inter-subject variability. This study investigates movement intention recognition from two complementary modalities EMG–IMU and EEG, under both subject-aware and cross-subject evaluation settings, with emphasis on how feature representations and evaluation protocols affect generalization. For EMG-IMU, we propose a recognition framework based on time-synchronized signal processing and multi-domain feature extraction, combined with a confusion-driven feature optimization strategy. By explicitly analyzing interclass confusion patterns, two feature sets are constructed for subject-aware and cross-subject scenarios. citation_details.title: Bayesian Complete-Pooling in Cross-Subject Classification for Motor Imagery Electroencephalogram
citation_details.author: Ethan Davis
citation_details.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have long sought calibration-free operation, yet classifiers are typically benchmarked on discrimination alone. Discrimination is blind to calibration, a meaningful gap given that electroencephalogram (EEG) signals are nonstationary and point-estimate classifiers can become overconfident under distribution shift. We conducted a large-scale study contrasting Bayesian complete-pooling models against frequentist baselines for cross-subject, left-hand versus right-hand motor imagery EEG classification across 20 datasets. Each of six frequentist pipelines was paired with an analogous Bayesian pipeline sharing identical feature engineering, fit via Markov chain Monte Carlo posterior sampling. Our primary metric was the Brier score, decomposed into reliability and resolution, alongside the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for discrimination and Shannon entropy for sharpness.
